key_insight: For low-Prandtl-number forced convection, only a few RANS heat-transfer closures are both robust and accurate, with k-ω SST plus the Kays Pr_t correlation performing best overall.
engineering_relevance: This helps CFD practitioners choose thermal turbulence models for liquid-metal heat transfer where standard momentum-thermal analogies break down.
method: Benchmarked multiple RANS thermal closures in OpenFOAM v2212.
Compared k-ω SST, four-equation k-ε-kθ-εθ, logarithmic k-Ω-kθ-Ωθ, and algebraic heat-flux models.
Validated against DNS and prior published results in channel flow, pipe flow, and heated backward-facing step flow.
evidence_signal: The models were assessed for reproducibility, robustness, and accuracy using DNS data and original-publication results across three canonical forced-convection test cases.
watch_item: Some closures showed weak numerical robustness or failed to reproduce published thermal fields, so implementation details and equation consistency are critical.
paper_title: Critical assessment of RANS Models for Turbulent Heat Transfer in Low-Prandtl-Number Forced Convection
